beds.title: Heated bed zones
beds.intro: The bed is a single one, split into zones. Define in the configuration the zones it needs: the sensor, the heater and the M140 P H link of each. You pick the pins among the free ones, see the exact lines and the file they go in, and create a plan with a backup; the board restarts to read it.

help.bed_what: The RRF zone number: the P of M140 P<n>. The bed is a single one; every zone is a heater with its own sensor.
help.bed_why: That way the service can split the temperature across the zones and you can adjust each one.
help.bed_missing: Without the zones defined the board only heats zone 0 and the others do not respond.
help.bed_how: Use the missing numbers (the 3D printing page sends you the ones of the zones the board lacks).
help.pins_what: The pins of the board: one for the temperature sensor and one for the output that switches the heater.
help.pins_why: Only free pins that fit that use are offered. The page never picks them for you.
help.pins_missing: A wrong pin could heat unattended or leave the bed unmeasured.
help.pins_how: Check them against your wiring before creating the plan. Every zone uses its own.
help.output_what: The pin of the board that switches the heater. A bed or heater MOSFET (out0 to out3) drives it directly; every other pin drives a relay.
help.output_why: The page deduces from the pin whether a relay is needed: with a board MOSFET it asks no type.
help.output_missing: A heater hung from a pin without a power MOSFET does not heat or damages the board.
help.output_how: Pick the pin the heater or the relay is wired to. out0 carries 18 A; out1 to out3, 6 A.
help.kind_what: What sits between the pin and the heater: a solid-state relay (AC or DC) or a mechanical relay.
help.kind_why: It sets the PWM frequency of the output (M950 Q): 10 Hz for a solid-state relay, no PWM for a mechanical one.
help.kind_missing: With the wrong type a mechanical relay chatters or a solid-state relay regulates badly.
help.kind_how: Look at the relay: AC if it switches mains, DC if it switches 24 V, mechanical if it has a coil.
help.max_what: The highest temperature the board lets that heater reach (M143).
help.max_why: It is the protection of the firmware: it cuts the heater if it goes over, whatever the service does.
help.max_missing: With a cap that is too high a sensor failure could let it heat too much.
help.max_how: Set it a little above your working temperature, for example 120 °C.
help.sensor_thermistor_what: A temperature sensor whose resistance changes with heat. The common bed one is 100 k, beta 3950.
help.sensor_thermistor_why: The board reads it on a dedicated temperature input (temp0 to temp3).
help.sensor_thermistor_missing: With the wrong type the temperature reads wrong and the bed over or under heats.
help.sensor_thermistor_how: Check the datasheet. If it is not the common one, pick another type or give its values.
help.sensor_pt1000_what: A platinum sensor of 1000 ohm at 0 C. Common in industrial and high temperature beds.
help.sensor_pt1000_why: The board reads it on a dedicated temperature input (temp0 to temp3).
help.sensor_pt1000_missing: On a thermistor setting it would read very wrong and could overheat the bed.
help.sensor_pt1000_how: Use it only if the sensor says PT1000. A PT100 is a different type.
help.sensor_thermocouple_what: A K thermocouple read by a MAX31855 chip, on the SPI bus. It reaches very high temperatures.
help.sensor_thermocouple_why: It needs the SPI expansion board (daughterboard) and the pin is its chip select (spi.cs).
help.sensor_thermocouple_missing: Without the chip and its board there is no reading and the heater will not start.
help.sensor_thermocouple_how: Check the chip is a MAX31855 and wired to the pin you pick.
help.sensor_pt100_what: A PT100 platinum sensor read by a MAX31865 chip, on the SPI bus. It is precise.
help.sensor_pt100_why: It needs the SPI expansion board (daughterboard) and the pin is its chip select (spi.cs).
help.sensor_pt100_missing: Without the chip and its board there is no reading and the heater will not start.
help.sensor_pt100_how: Check the chip is a MAX31865 set for PT100 and wired to the pin you pick.
help.edit_heater_what: The heater number of this zone: the H of its M950 and of M140 P<zone> H<n>.
help.edit_heater_why: The firmware links the zone to that heater, so it decides which output heats.
help.edit_heater_missing: A wrong number can leave the zone unheated or take another heater.
help.edit_heater_how: Pick it from the list: heaters another zone uses are greyed out, and free numbers are offered too.
help.edit_sensor_what: The sensor number this heater reads: the S of its M308 and the T of its M950.
help.edit_sensor_why: The firmware measures the zone with that sensor to keep its temperature.
help.edit_sensor_missing: A wrong sensor makes the heater regulate with another reading.
help.edit_sensor_how: Pick it from the list: sensors another zone uses are greyed out, and free numbers are offered too.
help.sensor_tc_max31856_what: A thermocouple read by a MAX31856 chip, on the SPI bus. It takes the types B, E, J, K, N, R, S and T.
help.sensor_tc_max31856_why: It needs the SPI expansion board (daughterboard) and the pin is its chip select (spi.cs). It has a 50 or 60 Hz filter.
help.sensor_tc_max31856_missing: Without the chip and its board there is no reading and the heater will not start. A wrong type reads a wrong temperature.
help.sensor_tc_max31856_how: Check the chip is a MAX31856 (two FAULT lights on the Duet3D board) and pick the letter of your thermocouple.
help.sensor_linear_analog_what: A sensor that gives a voltage proportional to the temperature (for example a thermocouple amplifier with an analog output).
help.sensor_linear_analog_why: The board reads the voltage on a temperature input or an io input and scales it between two values you give.
help.sensor_linear_analog_missing: Without a correct range the temperature reads wrong and the bed can overheat. That is why there are no default values.
help.sensor_linear_analog_how: Check the sensor sheet: write what it reads at 0 V and at full scale. Test it cold before heating.
help.therm_c_what: The C coefficient of the Steinhart-Hart model of a thermistor. Optional: blank is 0, which is normal for a bed.
help.therm_c_why: It refines the curve at high temperature. The E3D, for example, uses 7.06e-8 with beta 4725.
help.therm_c_missing: Without C the reading is a little off at high temperatures; on a bed it rarely matters.
help.therm_c_how: Copy it from the datasheet or from the Duet3D table. Scientific notation is fine: 7.06e-8.
help.tc_type_what: The letter of the thermocouple type: B, E, J, K, N, R, S or T. It is printed on the wire or its sheet.
help.tc_type_why: The chip turns the voltage into a temperature according to the type; K is the most common and the default.
help.tc_type_missing: With the wrong letter the temperature reads wrong even though the sensor works.
help.tc_type_how: Use the letter the thermocouple maker gives. If in doubt, the colour of the wire usually tells it.
help.mains_what: The frequency of the electric mains where you live: 50 Hz or 60 Hz.
help.mains_why: The readings are timed with it to reject the interference from the mains.
help.mains_missing: With the wrong frequency the reading has a little more noise, but it still works.
help.mains_how: Most of Europe, Africa and Asia use 50 Hz; North America uses 60 Hz.
help.wires_what: How many wires connect the PT100 to the board: 2, 3 or 4.
help.wires_why: The chip cancels the resistance of the wires according to the wiring. 3 wires must be told; 2 and 4 read the same.
help.wires_missing: With a number that is not the real one the reading rises about 2.5 degrees for each ohm of wire.
help.wires_how: Count the wires of the sensor and check the jumpers of the board: they must match what you pick here.
help.rtd_ref_what: The value, in ohm, of the reference resistor of the PT100 board.
help.rtd_ref_why: The chip measures the PT100 by comparing it with that resistor.
help.rtd_ref_missing: Blank uses the board's own (400 ohm on the Duet3D one). With a wrong value the temperature reads wrong.
help.rtd_ref_how: Leave it blank with the Duet3D board. Write it only with another board: it is printed on it (for example 430).
help.analog_range_what: What the reading is when the sensor gives 0 V and when it gives its maximum (full scale).
help.analog_range_why: The board spreads those two values linearly between 0 and the maximum voltage.
help.analog_range_missing: Without both values there is no reading. With wrong values the bed overheats.
help.analog_range_how: Write the ones of the sensor sheet (for example 0 and 300). The full scale one must be higher.
help.analog_filtered_what: Turns on the filter of the reading: slower but with less noise.
help.analog_filtered_why: The board can only filter on an input made for thermistors (temp0 to temp3).
help.analog_filtered_missing: With the filter on an io input the plan is refused; without the filter the reading is noisier.
help.analog_filtered_how: Leave it on with a temp input. With an io input, turn it off.

probe.title: Probe repeatability
probe.intro: Touches the same point several times and measures how much the height varies. A good probe repeats within hundredths of a millimetre.

probe.thresholds: Verdict: good up to {warn} mm, bad above {bad} mm standard deviation.

level.title: Bed levelling
level.intro: Measures the bed with the probe and, with several Z motors and M671, corrects it in passes until it is within tolerance.

mesh.err_taper: The taper height is a whole number between 0 and 50 mm.
mesh.err_name: Name of 1 to 32 characters: letters, numbers, hyphen and underscore.

mesh.tolerance_hint: Cells outside the tolerance from the mean get a dashed outline.

height.title: Tool height
height.intro: How the height of each mode is measured, the BLTouch trigger height, the fine adjustment and the paper. It applies to every zone.

height.not_current: The machine is not in {mode} mode now: you can change the fine adjustment and the method, but the probe measurements are only made in the active mode.
height.note_bltouch: BLTouch: it measures the surface at the Z point. Its trigger height (G31 Z) is one per mode; if the tool ends up too high or too low, use the fine adjustment.
height.note_paper: Paper: no probe. You take the tool to the point, lower it until it brushes a sheet and the height is set there.
height.note_szp: SZP (Duet scanning Z probe, FFF only): calibrates the drive level and the height against the reading.
height.from_mode_file: the one of the mode file
height.adjust_tip: Positive = the tool ends up further from the surface. It applies to every zone of the mode.
height.err_adjust: The adjustment must be between -3 and 3 mm.
height.err_paper: The thickness must be between 0 and 3 mm.
height.block_not_current: The machine has to be in {mode} mode to measure.
height.block_macro_missing: The calibration macros are missing on the card (zcal-*.g, installed by the Workbench plugin).
height.block_macro_missing_no_workbench: The calibration macros are missing on the card (zcal-*.g).
height.block_no_probe: The machine has no probe in this mode.
height.block_no_szp: There is no probe K1 (SZP) in this mode.
height.hook_missing: The mode files {files} do not load the calibration when the mode changes yet.
height.hook_tip: Adds an M98 line at the end of each mode file (a copy of the original is kept).
height.hook_done: Done: mode files updated ({files}). A copy of each was kept.
height.conflict: The calibration changed while you were editing it: it was read again, check the values and save once more.
height.not_applied_now: (it will apply on the next mode change: a job is running now or the board is not connected)
height.err_szp: S must be between 1 and 31 and R must be a whole number.
height.paper_marked: Z set with the paper: the tool rises to 5 mm.
height.wizard_paper_title: Measure the height with paper in {mode}
height.step_goto: Bring the tool over the point X {x} Y {y}.
height.step_lower: Lower it in small steps until it brushes the paper (Z now: {z}).
height.step_measure: The probe measures at the same point.
height.point_clamped: The point was moved inside the travel of the machine.
height.mark_k0: It brushes the paper: mark Z0 and rise
height.mark_paper: It brushes the paper: set Z with a {paper} mm paper
height.measured_text: It triggered at {med} mm (before {prev} mm). It is saved as the G31 Z of {mode}.
height.shift_warning: It changes by {d} mm: check the paper before saving.
height.szp_tip: With Z0 on the bed and the axes homed, it puts the SZP over the point and calibrates.

power.title: Power loss
power.intro: What the machine does when the supply drops (the M911 line of the configuration) and which files the firmware leaves to resume a job.
power.state_ok: All good: the machine has power-loss protection and no job was interrupted.
power.state_interrupted: A job was interrupted by a power cut (resurrect.g): check it before resuming.
power.state_no_line: The configuration has no M911 line: the machine does not react to a power cut.
power.state_unread: The configuration could not be read: what the machine does on a power cut is unknown.
power.line_help: When the voltage drops below the first value the machine saves the job and runs the commands below. It can only resume once the voltage rises above the second value, which must be higher. The change takes effect when the board restarts.
power.commands_label: Commands it runs on a cut
power.admin_hint: A wrong value can switch the machine off in the middle of a job or leave it unprotected: only an administrator changes it, with a preview.
power.plan_title: Power-loss voltages change: review before applying
power.err_number: Type two voltages: the first between {sMin} and {sMax} V and the second between {rMin} and {rMax} V.
power.err_order: The resume voltage must be higher than the trigger voltage.
power.truncated: Only the first {n} characters are shown.
power.resurrect_what: The firmware writes it while a job runs. It keeps which file it was, how far it got and where the axes were.
power.resurrect_none_help: It only appears if a job is cut. While it does not exist there is nothing to resume.
power.resume_hint: Resuming runs M916: the prologue first and then this file. The service checks everything again before sending it.
power.prologue_title: resurrect-prologue.g: what it does before resuming
power.prologue_what: The firmware runs it before resurrect.g. It decides what happens in each mode.
power.standard_yes: It is the workshop standard file.
power.standard_no: It differs from the workshop standard: it is respected as it is, this page does not change it.
power.fact_laser_asks: Laser: switches the tool off and asks for confirmation before going on.
power.fact_laser_no_ask: Laser: does NOT ask for confirmation before going on.
power.fact_cnc_asks: CNC: switches the tool off and asks for confirmation before going on.
power.fact_cnc_no_ask: CNC: does NOT ask for confirmation before going on.
power.fact_stops_tool: Switches the spindle or laser off (M5).
power.fact_no_stop: It does not switch the spindle or laser off (M5): the tool could start by itself when resuming.
power.fact_air_off: Switches the air pump off (M42 P7 S0).
power.fact_cancels: If you answer no, it cancels the job (M0).
power.fact_other_modes: 3D printing: resumes almost alone (waits for the temperature and re-homes X/Y).
power.fact_nothing: It has no rules per mode: it does nothing useful before resuming.
power.missing_text: Without it, a laser or CNC job would resume without switching the tool off or asking for confirmation. The workshop standard can be created: in laser and CNC it switches the tool off and asks; in 3D printing it resumes almost alone.
power.create_admin_only: Only an administrator creates it, with a preview.
power.chk_resurrect: There is a complete resurrect.g: the job and the point it reached.
power.chk_job_file: The job file is still on the card.
power.chk_idle: The machine is idle (not running, paused or halted).
power.chk_mode: The mode of the machine is known.
power.chk_supply: The supply is back above the restore voltage.
power.chk_prologue: resurrect-prologue.g exists (it switches the tool off and asks for confirmation in laser and CNC).
power.ack_piece: The part is where it was.
power.ack_tool: The tool is the right one and is held well.
power.ack_area: The area is clear and I can stop the machine.
power.resume_blocked: Something in the list is missing: it cannot be resumed yet.
power.resume_need_ack: Tick the three confirmations to be able to resume.
power.resume_sent: Command sent. The machine runs the prologue first and then the job; in laser and CNC it asks you to confirm again on the machine.
power.files_help: The firmware writes resurrect.g while a job runs; it is what resumes the job after a cut. resurrect-prologue.g runs first: in laser and CNC it asks for confirmation and switches the spindle and pump off.
power.resurrect_yes: exists: a job can be resumed ({job}).
power.resurrect_no: does not exist: no job was interrupted.
power.prologue_no: does not exist: resuming asks for no confirmation.

limits.title: Axis limits
limits.intro: The soft limits (M208) of each axis and the endstop verification.
limits.config_unread: The configuration could not be read: only the board values are shown.
limits.warn_bad_limits: The limits of this axis are not consistent.
limits.err_number: Type two numbers in millimetres (up to 5000).
limits.err_order: The minimum must be below the maximum.
limits.admin_hint: Wrong limits can crash the machine: only an administrator changes them, with a preview.
limits.verify_intro: Homes the axes (it moves them) and checks that each endstop was free before and that the axis ended where it should.

calibration.title: Calibration
calibration.intro: Assistants for steps per mm, squareness and backlash. Each one shows its sum, the service does the final calculation and the result is sent as a plan that is reviewed before applying.
calibration.motors_link: If a motor loses steps or the driver complains, look at the Motors page: here only measurements are calibrated.
calibration.err_no_current: The current steps per mm of this axis is not known.
calibration.field_positive: It must be a number greater than zero.
calibration.steps_send_help: It moves the axis relative and with no laser. It asks you to confirm first; the machine must be idle and the axis homed.
calibration.steps_send_max: Up to {max} mm are sent from here; for a longer move, run it yourself.
calibration.steps_send_axis: Only an axis is moved from here: an extruder is calibrated by extruding.
calibration.steps_sent: Move sent: {axis} {distance} mm. Measure how far it really moved and type the measured value.
calibration.err_positive: Type every value as a number above zero.
calibration.err_commanded: The commanded move must be between 1 and 5000 mm.
calibration.err_ratio: The change is too big (more than double or less than half): check the measurements.
calibration.err_side: The side of the square must be between 10 and 1000 mm.
calibration.err_diagonal: The diagonals do not match a square of that side: check the measurements.
calibration.err_implausible: A skew above 3 degrees is not plausible: check the measurements or fix the mechanics.
calibration.err_entry: Each row needs both readings, or to be empty.
calibration.err_sample: Each measurement must be between 0 and 2 mm, with at most 20 rows.
calibration.err_multiplier: The multiplier must be between 1 and 100.
calibration.steps_intro: Command a move of a known length, measure what the axis really travelled and the new value comes from the formula.
calibration.steps_big: The change is above 10 %: repeat the measurement to confirm it before applying.
calibration.steps_hint: The M92 line is written in the configuration, with a backup copy.
calibration.steps_plan: Steps per mm: review before applying
calibration.skew_intro: Draw a square with its two diagonals, measure the diagonals and their difference gives the skew between the two axes.
calibration.skew_d1: Diagonal from the origin to the opposite corner
calibration.skew_big: The skew is above 1 degree: fix the mechanics first (loose axes, twisted frame) and then compensate what is left.
calibration.skew_sign: Not verified on a real machine: repeat the square after applying and check that the diagonals become equal. If it gets worse, the sign is the other way round.
calibration.skew_hint: The M556 line is written in the configuration, with a backup copy.
calibration.backlash_intro: Bring the axis to a point from one side and from the other, write down the real position it reaches each time (with a dial gauge, for example) and repeat several times.
calibration.backlash_fixed: The M425 compensation is for FIXED backlash (couplings, nuts, pulleys). It does not fix belt stretch, which changes with speed and load.
calibration.backlash_stats: {n} measurement(s): mean {mean} mm, deviation {stdev} mm, minimum {min} mm, maximum {max} mm
calibration.warn_large_correction: The correction is above 10 %: repeat the measurement before applying.
calibration.warn_microstepping_note: M92 is microsteps per mm of the current M350: if you change the microstepping, this value changes with it.
calibration.warn_fixed_backlash_only: M425 is for fixed backlash only, not for belt stretch or flex.
calibration.warn_inconsistent: The measurements differ a lot from each other: the play is not constant (it may be belt stretch or a loose part). Compensating will not fix it.
calibration.warn_big_backlash: The backlash is above 0.5 mm: it is a mechanical fault worth fixing before compensating.
calibration.warn_per_motor: On CoreXY or other kinematics M425 is per MOTOR, not per axis: check the result.
calibration.warn_zero: The proposed value is zero: there would be nothing to compensate.
calibration.warn_not_in_g32: M425 is not applied to the levelling moves (G32).
calibration.warn_below_minimum: The frequency is below 4 Hz: check the count of ripples.
calibration.warn_very_high: The frequency is above 200 Hz: check the count of ripples.

motion.title: Motion parameters
motion.intro: Current, microstepping, speed, acceleration and jerk of each axis and extruder, as the board reports them.
motion.config_unread: The configuration could not be read: the driver mode may be missing.
motion.units: Current in mA, percentages in %, speed and jerk (M566) in mm/min, acceleration in mm/s², printing jerk (M205) in mm/s. A dash is a value the board does not report. * = interpolated, or default mode (the configuration does not set it).
motion.motors_question: Does a driver complain or does the motor lose steps?
motion.edit_intro: One parameter is changed at a time: the plan is prepared, the change in the file is reviewed and only then applied. Nothing is ever written to the driver directly.
motion.current_warn: More current heats the motor and the driver. Raise it little by little and watch the temperature. Profile cap: {max} mA.
motion.mode_hint: The mode is changed per driver, only if the M569 line already exists, and takes effect when the board restarts.
motion.admin_hint: Only an administrator changes these parameters.
motion.no_trial: This parameter cannot be tried without saving: it takes effect when the board restarts.
motion.mode_default: Default mode: the configuration does not set it
motion.err_choice: Choose one of the values in the list.

shaping.title: Input shaping
shaping.intro: Reduces vibration (ringing) after direction changes by filtering the motion with a resonance frequency of the machine (M593).
shaping.not_reported: The board does not report input shaping (firmware without support or not configured).
shaping.current_values: Type {type}, frequency {frequency} Hz, damping {damping}, minimum acceleration {accel} mm/s²
shaping.warn_retune_pressure_advance: With input shaping active it is worth tuning the pressure advance again.
shaping.warn_custom_shaper: The shaper is of the custom type: it is shown but not edited here, and cannot be put back by a trial.
shaping.min_accel_note: The minimum acceleration is shown as the board reports it; it is not edited from here.
shaping.tech_hint: The M593 line is written in the configuration, with a backup copy.
shaping.err_type: Choose a type from the list.
shaping.err_frequency: The frequency must be between {min} and 250 Hz.
shaping.err_damping: The damping must be a number from 0 up to below 1.
shaping.tuner_none: This machine has no accelerometer, so the frequency cannot be measured automatically. Use the ringing test below: print or mark the pattern, count the ripples and compute the frequency.
shaping.tuner_intro: The board reports {count} accelerometer(s). The collection moves the axis and saves the samples in a file (M955 and M956 on the service).
shaping.tuner_declared: The accelerometer is only declared in the profile, the board does not list it: the service will refuse the collection.
shaping.tuner_next: The service only collects the data: it does not compute the frequency. Read it from the data with the tool you prefer and type it in the form above.
shaping.ringing_intro: The service generates G-code of short strokes with abrupt stops at different accelerations. It is shown so you copy it and run it yourself as a job with the machine free: the page does not send it.
shaping.ringing_measure: After the test: count the ripples
shaping.ringing_no_freq: Type the ripples and the distance to compute the frequency.
shaping.err_ringing: Type speed, ripples and distance above zero.
shaping.err_ripples: The ripples must be a whole number between 2 and 200.

try.title: Try now
try.intro: Applies the value only for a while, without saving it. If you do not press Keep, the service puts the previous value back by itself.
try.running: Trial of {kind} running: it reverts by itself in {seconds} s.
try.keep_hint: Keep leaves the value active until the next start; afterwards you can prepare it as a permanent change.
try.needs_role: Your role does not allow trying this value.
try.done_kept: Value kept until the next start.
try.done_reverted: The previous value was put back.
try.done_expired: Time is over: the service put the previous value back.
try.err_try_pending: A trial is already running: end it first.
try.err_busy_run: A procedure is running: wait for it to end.
try.err_no_previous: The current value could not be read: nothing is tried without a way back.
try.err_not_found: The trial no longer exists (it may have ended).
try.err_revert_failed: The previous value could not be put back: check the machine.

maintenance.title: Maintenance
maintenance.intro: Hours and distance are counted by the service, not by the board. The plan lists what to service and when; mark an item as done when you do it.
maintenance.estimated_note: The distance is ESTIMATED from sampled positions and is always a little below the real one. Power-on hours count while the machine is powered and the motor is not released; movement hours count while the axis moves.
maintenance.no_history: Nothing has been marked as done yet.
maintenance.notify_on: A phone notice is sent when an item becomes due.
maintenance.notify_off: No phone notice when an item becomes due.
maintenance.not_counting: The service is not counting now (the Machine module is stopped or has no data).
maintenance.gaps: The service skipped {gaps} gap(s) in the data and {jumps} implausible jump(s) instead of counting them.
maintenance.cross_ok: Cross-check with the last job: estimated / planned path = {ratio} (as expected).
maintenance.cross_low: Cross-check with the last job: estimated / planned path = {ratio}: the sampling misses part of the movement.
maintenance.cross_high: Cross-check with the last job: estimated / planned path = {ratio}: more than planned, check the file or the noise.
maintenance.field_notify: Send a phone notice when an item becomes due
maintenance.err_id: The code needs lowercase letters, digits, dot, dash or underscore, starting with a letter.
maintenance.err_label: A name of up to 80 characters is needed.
maintenance.err_value: A number from 0.01 to 1000000 is needed.
maintenance.err_too_many: The plan has too many items.

verify.title: Verification with the camera
verify.intro: The camera measures where the head or a mark really is and compares it with where the offset says it should be.
verify.manual: The camera cannot measure on this machine (Vision does not offer vision.measure), so the verification is manual: mark a point at each offset and measure the difference with a ruler or a calibrated eye.
verify.moves_note: The machine moves while this runs; a laser mark is fired only with the laser method.
verify.system_note: Goes to the work origin of the system and compares it with what the camera sees there.
verify.tool_note: Uses the tool that is active now (the run never changes tool): its tip should land on the work origin of the current system.
verify.no_rows: No verification has been made yet.
verify.table_note: The latest result of each system or tool. The error is the distance between the measured and the expected point; the uncertainty is twice the camera's sigma.
verify.last_out: Out of tolerance: the offset does not point where the camera sees it.
verify.last_inconclusive: Inconclusive: the camera is not precise enough to decide. Improve its calibration or raise the tolerance.

bed.points_help: Tap the bed to add a point. Keyboard: Tab to a point, Enter selects it, arrows move it (Shift: ten steps), Delete removes it, Ctrl+Z undoes, Ctrl+Y redoes.
bed.note_outside_area: That spot is outside what the probe can measure, so no point was added.
bed.note_outside_reach: That spot is outside the probe reach, so no point was added.
bed.note_limit: No more points: the limit is {n}.
bed.note_duplicate: There is already a point there.
bed.note_seed_big: The grid has {n} points and only {max} can be chosen. Make the region smaller first.
bed.note_set_dropped: {n} points of the set were outside this bed and were left out.
bed.grid_title: The grid that will be measured
bed.grid_none: No points chosen yet: the region is measured as it is. Tap the bed to choose points.
bed.grid_none_all_ignored: None of the chosen points can be measured (they are outside what the probe can reach). Remove them or choose others.
bed.grid_none_no_room: There is no room next to these points for the second row or column the machine needs.
bed.grid_summary: The run will measure {nodes} nodes ({nx} x {ny}), spaced {sx} x {sy} mm.
bed.grid_extra: {n} of them are not points you chose: the machine measures a full regular grid and cannot skip a node inside it, so they complete it.
bed.grid_padded: The machine needs at least 2 rows and 2 columns, so a row or a column was added next to your points.
bed.grid_merged: {n} nodes carry more than one chosen point (the same place): they are measured once.
bed.grid_exact: Every chosen point is on a node.
bed.grid_inexact_too_many: A grid that holds every point exactly would need {nodes} nodes ({nx} x {ny}), more than a run takes ({max}). The best grid that fits is used, so some points move to the nearest node.
bed.grid_inexact_no_common_spacing: No regular grid holds all the points at once: their distances do not line up. The best grid is used, so some points move to the nearest node.
bed.grid_snapped_title: Points that move to a node
bed.grid_snapped: Chosen at X {x}, Y {y}: measured at the node X {nx}, Y {ny}, {d} mm away.
bed.grid_ignored: Chosen at X {x}, Y {y}: outside what the probe can measure, so it is not used.
bed.set_err_empty: Write a name for the set.
bed.set_err_long: The name can have 40 characters at most.
bed.set_err_no_points: There are no points to save.
bed.set_err_full: There are already 40 sets: delete one first.
bed.set_err_conflict: Somebody else changed the sets at the same time: try again.
bed.sets_intro: Named sets of points (for example the corners) kept on this machine, shared by Mesh and Level.
bed.sets_save: Save the points as a set
bed.sets_nothing_to_save: There are no points to save.
bed.sets_read_only: Your role can load sets but not save or delete them.
bed.sets_too_big: This set has more points than this page takes ({max}).
bed.sets_off_no_store: Point sets are off: the service of this machine does not have the store for them yet (it needs the newer WorkshopService).
bed.sets_off_error: Point sets are off: the service did not answer.
bed.job_intro: Type the area of a job, or drag it on the bed, to see whether the head can go there, the probe can measure there and the mesh covers it. Nothing moves.
bed.job_verdict_unknown: Cannot tell yet: some limits are not known.
bed.fit_unknown_no_bed: The axis limits are not known.
bed.fit_unknown_no_reach: The probe reach is not known.
bed.fit_unknown_no_mesh: There is no mesh: plan one or run one.
bed.fit_mesh_source_result: Checked against the mesh on show (the last result).
bed.fit_mesh_source_plan: Checked against the mesh the plan would measure.
bed.fit_share: {pct} % of the job is inside the mesh.

modes.title: Machine modes
modes.intro: Choose which kinds of work this machine does. Only the modes you switch on get steps, macros and settings in the plugins. Switching a mode off never deletes its files.
modes.profile_note: These switches only save in the machine profile which modes it uses. They do not change the mode the machine is in now.
modes.fff_about: Heated extruder printing. The 3D printing plugin follows this mode.
modes.alone_hint: This is the only mode you use, so there is nothing to configure. Switch on another one if you change heads on this machine.
modes.off_hint: Switched off: its files stay on the SD card, untouched.
modes.via_service: Saved in the machine profile (shared by every plugin and every screen).
modes.via_local: The service did not accept the change, so it is kept in this browser only. Ask a technician to save it for the whole machine.
modes.none_text: Select at least the modes you use. Until then the plugins do not show mode steps.
modes.files_note: Switching a mode off never deletes its macro or its settings file.
modes.needs_technician: Only a technician or an administrator can save the machine modes.
modes.use_suggested: Save the suggestion in the profile

workarea.title: Work area
workarea.intro: The part of the bed where the tool may work in each mode. The Work table draws it, the laser editor respects it and an origin outside it cannot be saved. It is measured by taking the tool by hand to two opposite corners, or typed.
workarea.intro_no_workbench: The part of the bed where the tool may work in each mode. It is measured by taking the tool by hand to two opposite corners, or typed.
workarea.mode_note: The area of {mode} is shown and changed. The mode in use now is {current}.
workarea.file_missing: There is no cutarea.g file yet: it is created when the first area is saved.
workarea.macros_missing: The corner macros are missing on the card (the Workbench plugin brings them): without them nothing can be measured or walked.
workarea.macros_missing_no_workbench: The corner macros are missing on the card: without them nothing can be measured or walked.
workarea.err_numbers: Type four numbers: X minimum and maximum, Y minimum and maximum.
workarea.err_small: The area is smaller than {min} mm on a side: it looks like a capture error.
workarea.err_outside: The area goes outside the travel of the axes ({reach}).
workarea.err_no_reading: The measurement did not leave a position. The reason is in the DWC console.
workarea.here_title: With the tool, using the jog
workarea.here_intro: Take the tool to the corner with the jog (any tool: laser, spindle, nozzle) and press the button: its position becomes the corner. Nothing moves.
workarea.err_not_homed_here: X and Y need a homing to know where the tool is.
workarea.saved_intro: Take the tool to a corner with the jog, save the position there, then to the opposite corner and save it too. Choose them here: nothing moves.
workarea.saved_none: There are no saved positions yet. Save them with the jog.
workarea.corners_intro: Two opposite corners of the area, with the tool. Measuring by hand releases X and Y (they have no force), you take the tool to the corner and the machine measures against the end stops; it ends with a homing of X and Y. Precision about ±0.4 mm.
workarea.release_hint: They lose their force and the position is lost. It asks for a confirmation.
workarea.released_note: X and Y are released. Take the tool to the corner, slowly, and press measure. Do not use the jog or other movement buttons: any movement enables them again by itself.
workarea.map_intro: Drag the handles or the rectangle to change the area, or draw a new one on the empty bed. A tap sets a corner or takes the tool to that point.
workarea.tool_goto_tip: With the laser off; it raises Z and lowers it on arrival.
workarea.map_legend_edit: Green dashed: the saved area. With handles: the one you are editing (the boxes above follow it).
workarea.mode_in_use: The mode the machine is in now.
workarea.fff_pointer_note: In FFF the tool is the nozzle (it may be hot): walking the area or taking it to a point raises Z 5 mm and moves it over the bed. Keep the way clear.
workarea.map_none: The travel of the axes is not known: the map cannot be drawn without it. Home the machine or check the M208 limits.
workarea.frame_intro: The tool walks the outline of the saved area, with the laser off, to see if it is the one you want.
workarea.frame_save_first: The saved area is walked: save the changes first.
workarea.block_loading: Reading the state of the machine…
workarea.block_macro_missing: The macro is missing on the card (the Workbench plugin brings it).
workarea.block_macro_missing_no_workbench: The macro is missing on the card.
workarea.block_not_homed: X and Y must be homed first.
workarea.block_no_area: This mode has no saved area.
workarea.block_not_edited: The machine is not in {mode} mode: only the area of the mode in use is walked.

toolwiz.title: Create a tool
toolwiz.intro: I lead you step by step to add a tool with its driver, heaters, fans and temperature sensors. Nothing is written to the machine until you review the exact lines and confirm; a backup is saved before writing.
toolwiz.mock_notice: Demo data: the service part is not installed yet. What you see here is an example and does not change the machine.
toolwiz.fix_first: Fix what is marked in red to continue.
toolwiz.type_intro: Pick the type: it decides what the tool can carry (driver, heaters, fans, sensors).
toolwiz.type_generic_about: One heater, one sensor and one fan.
toolwiz.file_note: A backup is saved before touching it.
toolwiz.name_intro: The number identifies the tool (T0, T1...). Only the free ones are offered.
toolwiz.carries_intro: A tool of type {type} can carry what you see below. Add only what it really has.
toolwiz.heaters_rule: A heater is never activated without a sensor, without a maximum temperature and without the autotune. This page switches nothing on: it writes it off.
toolwiz.max_hint: For this sensor, up to {n} C.
toolwiz.pins_intro: Only the free pins that fit each item are offered. One already used does not appear.
toolwiz.pin_no_free: No free pins left for this.
toolwiz.pins_used_note: These are not offered because something else already uses them.
toolwiz.preview_intro: These are the lines exactly as they will be written, and the file they go to. Nothing has been written yet.
toolwiz.warn_check_off_at_start: Check that the output starts off before connecting the power.
toolwiz.warn_heater_off_until_tuned: The heater stays off until you run the autotune.
toolwiz.apply_intro: First the plan is built (it writes nothing); you review it and only then apply it. A backup is saved before writing.
toolwiz.ack_autotune: I commit to run the autotune of every heater before using it.
toolwiz.ack_off: I will check that the output starts off before connecting the power.
toolwiz.plan_blocked: Something from the list above is missing.
toolwiz.plan_note: When applying, the service asks for a confirmation. Tools are read at start-up: the board will need a restart.
toolwiz.check_role: You are a technician: you can create tools.
toolwiz.block_role: You are not a technician: only a technician can create tools.
toolwiz.block_busy: The machine is working: wait for it to finish or stop it.
toolwiz.check_preview_stale: The preview is up to date.
toolwiz.block_preview_stale: You changed something after the preview: go back to it to see the new lines.
toolwiz.block_preview_errors: The preview has errors: fix them before creating.
toolwiz.check_heater_no_sensor: Every heater has its temperature sensor.
toolwiz.block_heater_no_sensor: A heater cannot be left blind without a sensor: pick its sensor.
toolwiz.check_heater_no_max: Every heater has its maximum temperature.
toolwiz.block_heater_no_max: Without a maximum temperature the heater is not protected: write it.
toolwiz.check_heater_max_range: The maximum temperature is in range.
toolwiz.block_heater_max_range: The maximum temperature must be between 50 and 450 C.
toolwiz.check_no_autotune: You committed to run the autotune.
toolwiz.block_no_autotune: A heater is not created without the commitment to run the autotune.
toolwiz.check_no_ack_off: You will check that the output starts off.
toolwiz.block_no_ack_off: Tick that you will check the output starts off before connecting the power.
toolwiz.err_name: The name is 1 to 32 characters, without quotes or semicolons.
toolwiz.err_tool_exists: Another tool already uses that number: pick a free one.
toolwiz.err_driver_used: That driver is not free: pick one from the list.
toolwiz.err_too_many: This tool does not allow that many.
toolwiz.err_heater_no_sensor: Pick the sensor of this heater.
toolwiz.err_heater_max_range: The maximum temperature goes from 50 to 450 C.
toolwiz.err_freq: The frequency goes from 1 to 65535 Hz.
toolwiz.err_rpm_range: The maximum speed goes from 1 to 100000 rpm.
toolwiz.err_power_range: The maximum power goes from 1 to 100 %.
toolwiz.err_laser_mode: The machine is not in laser mode.
toolwiz.err_pin_used: That pin is already used by {by}.
toolwiz.err_pin_unknown: That pin does not exist on the board.
toolwiz.err_pin_duplicate: You already gave that pin to something else in this tool.
toolwiz.err_preview_stale: The preview is not up to date: go back to it.
toolwiz.err_preview_no_max: The maximum temperature line (M143) of a heater is missing: cannot continue.
toolwiz.err_preview_activates: The preview has a line that switches something on: cannot continue.
toolwiz.err_not_applied: The plan has to be applied first.
toolwiz.err_values: Some value is not valid: check the previous steps.
toolwiz.err_other: The service refused something: check the previous steps.
toolwiz.tests_intro: The tool is written. Do each test by hand in this order and tick it. A heater is used only when its sensor reads right and its autotune is done.
toolwiz.tests_restart: Restart the board so it reads the new tool (M999) and only then continue with the tests.
toolwiz.tests_never: This assistant switches nothing on for you: you do the tests in DWC.
toolwiz.tests_all_done: All tests are done: the tool is ready to use.
toolwiz.test_blocked: It unlocks when you finish the previous test.
toolwiz.test_heat_note: This test heats: it asks for confirmation and is done with the machine watched.
toolwiz.test_restart_how: Send M999 from DWC (Console) and wait for the board to come back.
toolwiz.test_sensor_how: In DWC look at the sensor temperature: it must be near the shop temperature. If it shows 2000 or a crazy value, check the wire and the sensor type.
toolwiz.test_fan_how: In DWC raise the fan speed for a moment: it must spin and blow the right way. Then set it back to zero.
toolwiz.test_output_off_how: With the power disconnected, restart and check with a meter that the output is zero before connecting the power.
toolwiz.test_drive_how: Select tool T{tool} and move the extruder a few millimetres cold and without material: it must turn without forcing.
toolwiz.test_heater_how: Raise a few degrees from DWC with the machine watched and check that the sensor rises. If it does not, switch off and check the wiring.
toolwiz.test_autotune_how: Run the autotune of this heater in DWC and save the result. Until then do not use it to work.
toolwiz.h_type_what: The kind of tool: extruder, spindle, laser...
toolwiz.h_type_why: It defines which resources can be added and which lines are written.
toolwiz.h_type_missing: Without a type you cannot continue.
toolwiz.h_type_how: Tap the card that looks like what you installed.
toolwiz.h_file_what: The board configuration file, read at start-up.
toolwiz.h_file_why: That is where the board learns the tool exists.
toolwiz.h_file_missing: Without those lines the tool does not exist after a restart.
toolwiz.h_file_how: It is not chosen: the service decides and a backup is saved first.
toolwiz.h_number_what: The T number of the tool (T0, T1...).
toolwiz.h_number_why: You select the tool with it from DWC and from jobs.
toolwiz.h_number_missing: If you repeat one, the service rejects the plan.
toolwiz.h_number_how: Tap one of the free ones or type a number from 0 to 49.
toolwiz.h_name_what: A short name to recognise it.
toolwiz.h_name_why: It appears in DWC and in jobs.
toolwiz.h_name_missing: Without a name you cannot continue.
toolwiz.h_name_how: 1 to 32 characters, without quotes or semicolons.
toolwiz.h_driver_what: The driver (the motor output on the board) that moves the extruder.
toolwiz.h_driver_why: Without a driver the extruder does not move.
toolwiz.h_driver_missing: If it is missing, the tool is created but does not extrude.
toolwiz.h_driver_how: Pick a free one from the list; an axis driver is not offered.
toolwiz.h_output_what: The output that sends the speed or the power.
toolwiz.h_output_why: It is what switches the spindle or the laser on.
toolwiz.h_output_missing: Without it the tool cannot be controlled.
toolwiz.h_output_how: Frequency as the spindle or laser driver says; inverted only if its manual asks for it.
toolwiz.h_rpm_what: The maximum speed of the spindle.
toolwiz.h_rpm_why: 100 % of the output corresponds to this speed.
toolwiz.h_rpm_missing: Without it the speeds are not calculated right.
toolwiz.h_rpm_how: Read it on the spindle plate (rpm).
toolwiz.h_power_what: The maximum allowed power of the laser.
toolwiz.h_power_why: It limits what a job can ask for.
toolwiz.h_power_missing: Without it the laser cannot be created.
toolwiz.h_power_how: A percentage from 1 to 100; when in doubt, start low.
toolwiz.h_sensor_what: The sensor that measures the temperature.
toolwiz.h_sensor_why: The heater needs it to know when to stop.
toolwiz.h_sensor_missing: Without a sensor the heater is not created: it could heat without control.
toolwiz.h_sensor_how: Pick the type the manufacturer of the cartridge or thermistor says.
toolwiz.h_maxtemp_what: The highest temperature the heater may reach (M143).
toolwiz.h_maxtemp_why: If something fails, the board cuts the heater when it is exceeded.
toolwiz.h_maxtemp_missing: Without it the heater is not created.
toolwiz.h_maxtemp_how: A value slightly above your normal use, not beyond the sensor limit.
toolwiz.h_fan_why: It cools the part or the head.
toolwiz.h_fan_missing: Without it the tool is created anyway, without ventilation.
toolwiz.h_fan_how: The normal frequency is 250 Hz; inverted only if it behaves the opposite way.
toolwiz.h_pin_what: The board pin it is wired to.
toolwiz.h_pin_why: The board needs to know where each thing is.
toolwiz.h_pin_missing: Without a pin you cannot continue.
toolwiz.h_pin_how: Pick one from the list: only the free ones that fit this appear.
toolwiz.h_pin_sensor_what: The board input where the sensor goes.
toolwiz.h_pin_sensor_why: It is where the board reads the temperature.
toolwiz.h_pin_sensor_missing: Without a pin the sensor does not read.
toolwiz.h_pin_sensor_how: Thermistors and PT1000 go to a temperature input; the others to a SPI chip.
toolwiz.h_preview_what: The configuration lines that will be written.
toolwiz.h_preview_why: Seeing them first lets you check it is what you want.
toolwiz.h_preview_missing: If there are errors it cannot be created: go back to the step it says.
toolwiz.h_preview_how: Read them; the green line is the maximum temperature.
toolwiz.h_checks_what: The list of conditions that must be met to create.
toolwiz.h_checks_why: They are the safety rules: they cannot be skipped.
toolwiz.h_checks_missing: While any is red, the plan is not created.
toolwiz.h_checks_how: Fix what each red line says.
toolwiz.h_autotune_what: The automatic tuning of the heater temperature control.
toolwiz.h_autotune_why: Without it the heater can overshoot or never reach the target.
toolwiz.h_autotune_missing: Without the commitment the heater is not created.
toolwiz.h_autotune_how: After the restart, the last step guides you.
toolwiz.h_off_what: That the spindle or laser output starts off.
toolwiz.h_off_why: An output that starts on is dangerous.
toolwiz.h_off_missing: Without the tick it is not created.
toolwiz.h_off_how: Measure it with the power disconnected.
toolwiz.h_apply_what: It builds the plan: it shows the file and the changes, without writing.
toolwiz.h_apply_why: It is the final review with a backup before touching the machine.
toolwiz.h_apply_missing: If something changed, the plan is dropped and has to be built again.
toolwiz.h_apply_how: Press the button; then review and apply. The service asks for confirmation.
